title: filters: do not index an empty container command
body:
podman ps --filter command=<value> panics with "index out of range [0] with length 0" when any container in the store has no command recorded. GenerateContainerFilterFuncs indexes Container.Command()[0] without first checking the length.

A container has no command whenever it was created without an explicit command and the image contributed no CMD. Passing --entrypoint on its own is the shortest way to get there:

    podman create --name t --entrypoint /bin/true alpine
    podman ps -a --filter command=true

specgenutil.FillOutSpecGen only sets SpecGenerator.Command when a command was given on the command line, CreateContainer only calls WithCommand when that field is non-nil, and the image CMD fallback in container_internal.go is skipped once an entrypoint is set, so config.Command stays empty. An image that declares an ENTRYPOINT and no CMD reaches the same state without passing any flag, and nothing rejects such a container at creation time.

The filter is used by podman ps, by the libpod and Docker-compat /containers/json endpoints and by podman auto-update --filter, so one container of this shape breaks container listing for the whole store. On the CLI the command aborts with a stack trace; over the API the panic handler turns it into a 500.

Skip containers that have no command, which is what the other readers of this field already do in completion.go, container_inspect.go and container_exec.go. The external container variant of the filter indexes the same way. It cannot be reached today because ListStorageContainer always fills a command in, but guard it identically so the crash cannot reappear if that ever changes.
